extracted.intended_audience: funding organizations, academic institutions, center directors, and evaluators responsible for assessing interdisciplinary research and teaching
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for assessing outcomes, people, programs, and centers that engage in interdisciplinary research and interdisciplinary education. Covers direct and indirect impacts, evaluation methods, reviewer composition, and program-review categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measures of quality, relevance, and leadership (COSEPUP framework)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures do exist: measures of quality, in terms of research advancement; relevance, in terms of application development; and leadership, in terms of the ability to take advantage of opportunities when they arise, as evaluated by experts and users of research. Human-resource development is also a key outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use expert and user evaluation to assess quality (advances in knowledge), relevance (applications/translation), and leadership (capacity to capitalize on opportunities). Also track human-resource development (training, skills). These are not strictly annual productivity metrics but outcome-focused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field-based productivity metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect or field-based measures such as numbers of patents, publications, and citations; the prestige of universities, funding agencies, and journals; and approval of peers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These common bibliometric and prestige indicators are useful but insufficient alone for IDR. Use them in combination with more substance-focused and cross-disciplinary measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of relation to antecedent disciplinary knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: The degree to which new interdisciplinary work relates to antecedent disciplinary knowledge — credibility is often judged by consistency with the 'disciplinary canon' (often in more than one field).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether interdisciplinary contributions are grounded in and coherent with relevant disciplinary bodies of knowledge in the involved fields; high-quality IDR requires a unique coordination of disciplinary insights, not merely a sum of rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensible balance in weaving disciplinary perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: The sensible balance reached in weaving perspectives together — interdisciplinary work should thoughtfully balance the perspectives of the disciplines represented even when disciplinary standards conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the work integrates perspectives in a way that is defensible given differing disciplinary norms, and whether trade-offs between discipline-specific standards are acknowledged and managed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness in advancing understanding and inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: The effectiveness with which a particular piece of work advances understanding and inquiry — contributions oriented toward pragmatic problem solving and product development place a premium on standards of viability; algorithmic models are judged on simplicity and predictive power; multidimensional phenomena on comprehensiveness and empirical grounding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose evaluation criteria that match the work's aims (theory-building vs. problem-solving). For models, favor simplicity and predictive accuracy; for applied work, assess viability and empirical grounding; for broad phenomena, evaluate comprehensiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation relative to the drivers of IDR
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider IDR in light of its driving forces: the inherent complexity of nature and society; the drive to explore interfaces of disciplines; the need to solve societal problems; and the stimulus of generative technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how well a program addresses the relevant drivers for its mission: e.g., does it tackle complexity requiring multiple disciplines; does it truly explore interfaces and foster collaborations; does it produce practical solutions for societal problems; does it develop technologies that enable cross-field advances?

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct contributions to knowledge (new knowledge, new fields)
rubrics_metrics.description: Look for direct contributions in the form of new knowledge: stimulating new understanding in multiple fields, creation of new fields or disciplines, adding value to traditional fields, and development of new technologies or products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document examples such as creation of new research areas (e.g., computational biology), cross-fertilization of disciplinary methods, new instrumentation or products, and cases where IDR has driven breakthroughs across multiple disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect contributions to knowledge and practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect but substantial contributions such as information-sharing networks, congressional testimony, public-policy initiatives, mass-media placements, alternative-journal publications, long-term product development, and improvements to industrial products/processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture outputs beyond standard publications: policy influence, outreach, technology transfer, and nontraditional dissemination channels. These may require qualitative documentation and tracking over longer time horizons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information-sharing networks and social-network indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Use social network analysis to model structure, relations, and positions of research networks; identify hot spots of interdisciplinary activity, connectivity across disciplines, key personnel (nodes), and patterns of interaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect survey, bibliometric, observational, and interview data to map collaborations and identify who fosters interdisciplinarity. Note limitation: social network analysis reveals interactions but does not directly link interactions to performance outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of educational experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate enrichment of undergraduate and graduate education, including increased enrollments in IDR fields, enhanced non-majors' understanding of science and engineering, and attraction of broader student populations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track enrollment trends, degree completions, curriculum changes, student-level learning outcomes (scientific/technological literacy), and evidence that interdisciplinary programs attract different or more students to STEM fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhancement of institutional reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether interdisciplinary efforts enhance an institution’s reputation by establishing high-quality programs in cutting-edge, niche fields, thereby improving ability to attract students and faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document awards, named centers, successful recruitments, and external recognition attributable to interdisciplinary initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated value of shared instrumentation or tools
rubrics_metrics.description: IDR may demonstrate the value of major tools or instrumentation that have multiple applications (e.g., synchrotron radiation's broad impact).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the cross-disciplinary uptake of instruments/techniques, evidence of new applications enabled, and facilitation of collaborations around shared resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student outcomes for undergraduates and graduates
rubrics_metrics.description: Are students working with and learning from students in other disciplines; developing mastery of more than one discipline; developing a sense of how to integrate disciplines; learning instrumentation or techniques outside their home discipline?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use surveys, interviews, curriculum records, and demonstrated skills/products to assess multidisciplinary mastery, teamwork, cross-training, and career trajectories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postdoctoral scholar outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Do postdocs apply their expertise to add value to projects and to their own multidisciplinary grasp; can they interact with specialists in other disciplines and learn other disciplinary languages, content, and cultures?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate postdoc roles in projects, collaborative outputs, evidence of cross-disciplinary skill acquisition, and subsequent career placements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty evaluation for interdisciplinary contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions to frame faculty evaluation: Are faculty doing high-quality interdisciplinary work reported in leading journals/conferences? Are they working on topics beyond their original discipline? Have they extended their expertise or helped establish subfields? Do they include students/faculty from other disciplines? Are they evaluated by multidisciplinary review groups? Have they received recognition or invitations outside their discipline?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt multidisciplinary review panels for promotion/tenure; document cross-disciplinary publications, student supervision across departments, interdisciplinary awards, and external invitations as evidence of impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use both internal and external review including site visits
rubrics_metrics.description: At the heart of any evaluation process must be not only stringent peer review but also site visits that include personal interviews and objective observations. Both internal and external reviews are essential to combine familiarity with institutional processes and objectivity of independent observation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine written reviews, panel deliberations, and on-site visits with interviews and observations. Use external reviewers for objectivity and internal reviewers for institutional context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of external review groups (represent all appropriate sectors)
rubrics_metrics.description: External review groups should represent all appropriate sectors; for university centers, include 'users' of research outputs (industry, government, policy representatives) along with disciplinary and interdisciplinary experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select reviewers to provide depth of expertise in core and related disciplines and experience carrying out IDR; include nonresearch stakeholders when relevant to program goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of 'sunset' or evolution options for centers
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation that future directions for interdisciplinary centers include a 'sunset' option since initiatives will not be equally productive or long-lived; reviewers should consider whether the IDR effort is generating relevant new knowledge and whether it should be terminated or moved in a new direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess productivity and field evolution; plan phased transitions (e.g., rechartering as a new center) or termination when original goals have been met or priorities have shifted.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERC program-review categories (systems vision & value added)
rubrics_metrics.description: Renewal reviews are divided into categories including systems vision and value added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the center articulates a coherent systems vision and whether it adds value beyond individual projects; examine strategic alignment with broader goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERC program-review categories (strategic research plan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Renewal reviews include assessment of the strategic research plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess clarity of research priorities, coherence of long-term strategy, and adaptability across review periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERC program-review categories (research program)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research program evaluation: e.g., years 1-3 'Thrust team is appropriately cross-disciplinary, projects are becoming interdependent within the thrust and contributing to other thrusts' (high quality) vs. 'Thrusts and projects are single-disciplinary and isolated' (low quality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine team composition, cross-disciplinary interdependence, role of projects across thrusts, and trajectory across review cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERC program-review categories (education and educational outreach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Education & outreach evaluation: examples include cross-disciplinary research culture developing, students working in teams, and graduate-to-undergraduate ratio benchmarks (e.g., at most 2:1) as high-quality indicators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess curricular innovations, team-based student experiences, outreach activities, and student demographics; track progress across review periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERC program-review categories (industrial-practitioner collaboration & technology transfer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate industrial/practitioner collaboration and technology transfer as a distinct review category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document industry partnerships, technology transfer outcomes, impact on partners, and evidence that research meets industrial/practitioner needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERC program-review categories (strategic resource and management plan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess strategic resource allocation and management planning for the center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate sustainability plans, resource mobilization, management structures, and ability to become self-sustaining after award periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment methods for interdisciplinary training programs (IGERT example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Common assessment methods used in IGERT programs (listed by prevalence): informal feedback to PI/committee (84%), annual or more frequent surveys of trainees (68%), annual faculty assessment meetings (58%), participant meetings (57%), faculty surveys (33%), interviews/observation by external evaluator (30%), continuing observation by external evaluator (14%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a mix of formative and summative methods, include internal and external evaluators, and combine surveys, meetings, interviews, and observations to capture program functioning and trainee outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements of periodic self-assessment reports (Dutch assessment model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-assessment reports should include: characterization of the institute (mission, collaborations, affiliations); leadership (structure, programs, leaders); research strategy (context, short/long-term plans); researchers (personnel policy—selection, training, career planning, mobility); resources and funding; processes to support research (teamwork, PhD supervision, QA); reputation (citation scores, prizes, awards); internal assessment; external appreciation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require self-assessments every three years and external review every six years (example); ensure reports are comprehensive and support external evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal-review mechanisms ensure appropriate breadth and depth (Recommendation E-3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding orgs should enhance proposal-review mechanisms to ensure appropriate breadth and depth of expertise in review of proposals for IDR; involve researchers experienced with interdisciplinarity and representation of important disciplinary points of view; include nonresearchers when relevant; consider separate written contributions from disciplines for panel consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design review panels with interdisciplinary experience and disciplinary depth, solicit written inputs from constituent disciplines, and include stakeholder perspectives for applied problems to reduce bias and improve fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include interdisciplinary contributions in comparative institutional evaluations (Recommendation E-4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparative evaluations (e.g., departmental rankings) should include contributions of interdisciplinary activities that involve more than one department (even if double-counting), and experiment with matrix evaluation to capture cross-department accomplishments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey emerging fields for demographics and activities, implement matrix approaches that make cross-departmental efforts visible, and include mentoring, multi-department contributions, and publication impact across audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and credit criteria for interdisciplinary researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Include publication criteria such as nature of journal audiences, citation analysis that reveals broad interdisciplinary interest, 'double counting' credit to all coauthors, and analysis of multiple-authorship patterns revealing disciplinary backgrounds of coauthors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt promotion/assessment policies to recognize cross-disciplinary impact (e.g., give credit for interdisciplinary citation reach, joint authorship, and work published for multiple audiences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include facilitation of interdisciplinarity in accreditation and rankings
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations to include facilitation of interdisciplinarity as part of accreditation processes and comparative evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accreditors and ranking bodies should incorporate metrics and evidence of institutional support for interdisciplinarity (programs, centers, curricular integration, resource allocation).
